u.c: Proposed amendatory section.
u.s: The proposal amends WAC 392-425-040, Student eligibility.

u.c: Proposed WAC 392-425-040(1); program must be offered by an eligible local education agency; both listed child criteria apply.
u.s: Children satisfying the screening-benefit and age criteria are eligible to participate in TK.

u.c: Proposed TK eligibility criterion, together with the age criterion.
u.s: The local education agency must have determined through a screening process and tool that the child benefits from additional preparation for kindergarten.

u.c: Proposed TK eligibility criterion, together with the screening-benefit criterion.
u.s: A child must be at least four years old by August 31st of the school year of TK enrollment.

u.c: Age qualification for the school year of TK enrollment; cutoff clock not stated; timezone not stated; receipt-versus-dispatch not applicable because this is an age attainment date,
u.r: The age cutoff's clock and timezone are absent.
u.s: August 31st of the enrollment school year is the age-qualification cutoff.

u.c: Proposed WAC 392-425-040(1); eligible local education agency's TK program.
u.s: The screening-benefit determination and minimum-age criterion jointly define child eligibility, rather than alternatives.

u.c: Proposed WAC 392-425-040(2); when determining eligibility and admitting TK students.
u.s: Local education agencies must prioritize children most in need of additional preparation for kindergarten success, as demonstrated through a screening process and tool.

u.c: Proposed WAC 392-425-040(2); when determining eligibility and admitting TK students; children not otherwise eligible and not enrolled in another local program.
u.s: Local education agencies must give priority to children with the lowest family income.

u.c: Proposed WAC 392-425-040(2); when determining eligibility and admitting TK students; eligible child; disability alone is the basis.
u.s: Local education agencies must not exclude an eligible child from participation due only to a disability.

u.c: Proposed WAC 392-425-040(2); when determining eligibility and admitting TK students; eligible child; disability alone is the basis.
u.s: Local education agencies must not establish a policy prohibiting an eligible child's participation due only to a disability.

u.c: Deletion shown by double parentheses in proposed WAC 392-425-040(2)(d).
u.s: The proposal deletes WAC 392-425-040's prohibition on charging tuition or other fees to state-funded eligible students for TK enrollment.

u.c: Proposed WAC 392-425-040(2)(d); eligible local education agencies; no fee for children eligible but not yet placed in the early childhood education or assistance program or head スタ
u.s: The proposal adds sliding-scale TK enrollment fee authorization to WAC 392-425-040, subject to its listed no-fee exceptions.

u.c: Proposed rule; eligible local education agencies; excludes children eligible for but not yet placed in the early childhood education or assistance program or head start program, or
u.s: Eligible local education agencies are authorized to charge sliding scale fees for TK enrollment, subject to the separately stated no-fee exceptions.

u.c: Proposed WAC 392-425-040(2)(d)(i); children eligible for but not yet placed in the early childhood education or assistance program or the head start program.
u.s: Eligible local education agencies may not charge TK enrollment fees to children in this unplaced-program-eligible category.

u.c: Proposed WAC 392-425-040(2)(d)(ii); children with disabilities entitled to free appropriate public education in accordance with the federal individuals with disabilities education
u.s: Eligible local education agencies may not charge TK enrollment fees to children with disabilities entitled to free appropriate public education under the federal individuals with disabilities education act and chapter 28A.155 RCW.

u.c: Proposed WAC 392-425-040(2)(e); tuition and fees collected for students in classrooms receiving state funding for TK; in accordance with school district accounting manual requirem
u.s: Local education agencies must account separately for tuition and fees collected for students in state-funded TK classrooms, in accordance with the school district accounting manual.
WAC 392-425-065 is titled Allocation of state funding.

u.c: Proposed new section.
u.s: The proposal adds WAC 392-425-065, Allocation of state funding.

u.c: Proposed WAC 392-425-065; based on RCW 28A.300.072 and state omnibus budget requirements.
u.s: State TK funding will be allocated to eligible local education agencies; the allocating actor is not specified in this provision.

u.c: Proposed WAC 392-425-065(1); eligible local education agencies that received state TK allocations in the previous year.
u.s: Prior-year TK funding recipients will have priority for the subsequent year's state funding allocations.

u.c: Proposed WAC 392-425-065(2); when state funding is insufficient to maintain the number of students served in the subsequent year.
u.s: Eligible local education agencies will receive allocations based on one or more listed criteria; the allocating actor is not specified.

u.c: Proposed funding criterion under the insufficiency condition; one or more criteria may be used.
u.s: Districtwide percentage of students eligible for free and reduced price lunch is a TK funding allocation criterion.

u.c: Proposed funding criterion under the insufficiency condition; one or more criteria may be used.
u.s: Districtwide percentage of students eligible for special education services is a TK funding allocation criterion.

u.c: Proposed funding criterion under the insufficiency condition; one or more criteria may be used.
u.s: Districtwide percentage of students eligible for transitional bilingual program services is a TK funding allocation criterion.

u.c: Proposed funding criterion under the insufficiency condition; one or more criteria may be used.
u.s: Available data measuring access to state-funded early learning programs is a TK funding allocation criterion.

u.c: Proposed funding criterion under the insufficiency condition; one or more criteria may be used.
u.s: Local education agencies serving 20 or fewer TK students are a TK funding allocation criterion.

u.c: Proposed WAC 392-425-065(2); when state funding is insufficient to maintain the number of students served in the subsequent year.
u.s: Funding allocations to eligible local education agencies will use one or more of the five listed criteria, permitting individual criteria or combinations without specifying selection or weights.
